title: Kinematics: Constant Acceleration and Velocity–Time Graphs
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Kinematics Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use fundamental quantities and units in the SI system; displacement, velocity, acceleration; velocity–time graphs, including the gradient as acceleration and the area as displacement; the formulae for constant acceleration (suvat); motion under gravity.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on kinematics: suvat equations, velocity–time graphs, free fall under gravity and constant acceleration problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as.
key_sub: Gradient of a v–t graph = acceleration; area = displacement.
body_html:
How it works

For constant acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, s = ½(u + v)t. Under gravity a = g = 9.8 m/s².

Example

From rest, 2 m/s² for 5 s. Distance?

s = 0 + ½ × 2 × 25

Answer: 25 m

Common mistakes

  • Using s = vt when the speed is changing.
  • Forgetting to square t in ½at².
  • Using the wrong sign for g.

faq.q: Which suvat equation should I use?
faq.a: List s, u, v, a and t. Choose the equation that has the three you know and the one you want.

faq.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph show?
faq.a: The displacement (distance travelled in one direction).
